title: Universality beyond the Kibble-Zurek mechanism in the condensation of coherently coupled Bose gases
authors: Subhadeep Patra, Paolo Comaron, Arko Roy
abstract: We study the universal spatial statistics of point-like topological defects formed during the nonequilibrium condensation of a coherently coupled Bose gas using the stochastic projected Gross-Pitaevskii equation. The symmetry-breaking transition is driven by a linear quench of the chemical potential, leading to stochastic vortex nucleation in the individual condensate components. When the two components are considered together, these elementary defects may combine across components to emerge as composite topological defects known as full quantum vortices. Beyond the mean defect density predicted by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM), we investigate the spatial organization of both the elementary and composite defects and show that their positions are well described by a Poisson point process, revealing a universal stochastic geometry. This universality is further described through Voronoi tessellation, whose cell-area statistics follow Poisson-Voronoi predictions. We also introduce the spatial form factor for characterizing the vortex configurations and demonstrate the emergence of a characteristic dip-ramp-plateau structure. Our results establish universal stochastic geometry of topological defects beyond conventional Kibble-Zurek scaling and identify it as a fundamental feature of nonequilibrium condensation in coherently coupled Bose gases.
summary: The paper investigates how topological defects form during the non-equilibrium condensation of a coherently coupled Bose gas. By analyzing defect statistics using advanced tools like Poisson Point Processes and Spatial Form Factors, the authors demonstrate that the resulting spatial organization exhibits universal geometry beyond standard Kibble-Zurek scaling. This establishes a fundamental statistical description for defect formation in such quantum systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the universal spatial statistics of topological defects formed during the non-equilibrium condensation of a coherently coupled Bose gas, aiming to establish physics beyond standard Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM) predictions.
main_result: The defect positions are found to follow a homogeneous Poisson point process (PPP), revealing a universal stochastic geometry that persists even when considering composite topological defects. This universality is confirmed by analyzing Voronoi tessellation and the Spatial Form Factor (SFF).
method: The analysis employs the stochastic projected Gross-Pitaevskii equation (SPGPE) framework, combining theoretical scaling arguments with advanced tools from stochastic geometry like PPP modeling, Poisson-Voronoi tessellation, and SFF calculations.
model_or_system: The system is a coherently coupled Bose gas in two hyperfine states undergoing a quench driven by a linear variation of the chemical potential. The dynamics are modeled using the SPGPE for a 2D system.
key_observables: Topological defects (elementary and composite Full Quantum Vortices, FQVs); defect density ($ho$); equilibration time ($t_{eq}$); Poisson point process statistics; Voronoi cell area distribution; Spatial Form Factor (SFF).
important_parameters: Quench rate ($	au_Q$), coupling strength ($\Omega$), and the ratio of components' interactions ($g_{12}/g$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are projected onto low-energy modes via SPGPE, and the underlying spatial statistics are assumed to be well described by a Poisson Point Process (PPP).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate condensate norm growth and equilibration time scaling; they also show pair-distance distributions, nearest-neighbor spacing histograms conditioned on topological charge, and SFF plots comparing numerical results against analytical PPP predictions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the non-equilibrium dynamics (determining $t_{eq}$), then analyzing defect numbers ($\langle N angle$) via KZM scaling, and finally delving into spatial statistics using PPP, Voronoi tessellation, and SFF to prove universal geometric organization.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous quantitative framework for characterizing the emergent geometry of defects in interacting quantum systems, extending fundamental concepts like KZM into regimes involving multiple coupled components. The use of SFF connects condensed matter physics to spectral analysis techniques from quantum chaos.

Each curve is averaged over R = 100 stochastic trajectories. Black triangles mark the equilibration time teq. (b) Equilibration time teq as a function of the quench time τQ. Fits in the range τQ = 30–1000 show good agreement with Kibble–Zurek scaling, teq ∼τ 0.47±0.002 Q . Inset: Growth of the condensate norm N versus the scaled time t/√τQ. For t < teq, the curves collapse onto a universal form for all τQ except the fastest quench τQ = 5, consistent with Kibble–Zurek behavior.
